subject: Post-demo: Decision criteria, security path, and ally enablement
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@borealtech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Decision criteria, security path, and ally enablement

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with Boreal's evaluation rhythm: 

1) Decision criteria we heard (please flag anything missing):
   - Performance: p95 latency < 300ms, sustained throughput for 6k QPS during peak batch windows
   - Cost: target unit cost <$0.002/token at expected traffic profile
   - Security & compliance: SOC 2 in progress, ability to host in customer VPC, key management controls
   - Ops: model version pinning, traceability, and audit logs retention for 12 months

2) Security/procurement asks you raised:
   - SOC 2 report or interim evidence (currently you will accept our SOC 2-in-progress checklist)
   - Data flow diagram and retention policy
   - Sample contract clauses for data residency & liability

3) Proposed internal ally(s): you mentioned Jordan (product) as the technical sponsor and Linda Park (head of procurement) as the procurement contact. If there's an economic buyer we should engage, would that be Sam Ortiz (VP Product) or someone on the engineering leadership team?

4) Next steps (timeline):
   - I will send a focused one-pager for your internal ally that contains 3 talk tracks (cost, performance, security) by EOD Monday. (ACTION: Aisha)
   - Vivek will prepare a short ROI sketch (TCO comparison vs current infra) and a technical appendix for procurement. (ACTION: Vivek, ETA Tue)
   - You to share procurement contact email and any specific vendor questionnaire template. (ACTION: Jordan)

Attachments: Ill attach the ROI one-pager and a security evidence index for quick handoffs to procurement.

If that plan looks good, Ill also draft an internal email template Jordan can forward to Linda and Sam.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

Aisha —

Thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications:

- Economic buyer is likely Sam Ortiz (cc'ing him separately will help). He cares most about unit economics and time-to-value.
- Procurement contact is procurement@borealtech.com (Linda is the day-to-day but procurement mailbox owns vendor onboarding)
- For security, the SOC 2 in-progress checklist is fine for the initial review. We'll need the data flow diagram and KMS/HSM integration details for our security team.

Timeline: Linda and I are aiming to have vendor shortlisting done by July 9th. If you can get the ROI sketch and the one-pager this week, well circulate internally.

Also: could you include an expected rollout sequence (pilot -> phased rollout -> production) and an estimated ramp cost for months 1-6? That will help Sam make the economic case.

Jordan

Jordan / Aisha —

Attaching a short ROI sketch and rollout sequence as requested (attachment stubs below). High-level notes for Sam and the economic thread:

- Baseline: Boreals current hosted throughput costs ~ $45k/month (inferred from demo numbers).
- Redwood forecast (pilot month): $28k/month with pilot config (reduced tokens via caching + batching).
- Month 1-6 ramp: projected 20% month-over-month traffic growth; cumulative spend breaks even against migration dev effort by month 4 in our scenario.

Talk tracks for internal ally (Jordan / Sam):
  - Performance: p95 at targeted latency without engineering rework (we handle KV cache & batching)
  - Cost: expected 35-40% unit cost reduction vs current managed endpoint at production volumes
  - Security: private deployment option (VPC), KMS integration, and audit log retention configurable to 12 months

Quick pilot proposal (one paragraph you can paste into an internal email):
"Pilot (6 weeks): integrate Redwood Dedicated with a single model endpoint for Boreal search, run mirrored traffic for weeks 1-2, enable caching and measure unit cost changes in weeks 3-4, and cutover for read paths in week 6 if KPIs met (latency < 300ms, unit cost reduction >= 30%)."

Ive included the rollout table and cost sketch as files: Redwood-Boreal-ROI-onepager.pdf, rollout-cost-grid.xlsx (attachment stubs). Let me know if you want a shorter variant for execs.

—Vivek
